programs.name: Master of Laws (LLM)
programs.entry_requirements: A first law degree (JD or equivalent) is required. finance.costs_breakdown_note: Official 2026-27 undergraduate standard student budget for Autumn, Winter, and Spring: tuition USD 67,731; housing/food and other living figures are estimates/allowances, not a program price or net price. New students pay one-time orientation USD 525 and document fee USD 250. Cardinal Care is separately charged unless eligible comparable coverage is approved; international students are budgeted for this insurance.

financial_aid.merit_based_note: Undergraduate financial aid is 100% need-based. Stanford does not award academic or athletic merit scholarships for general undergraduate admission. (NCAA Division I athletic grants-in-aid are awarded independently).
financial_aid.need_policy_international_note: CRITICAL: Stanford is NEED-AWARE for international undergraduate applicants. Financial need is factored into the admissions decision. International applicants must apply for financial aid concurrently with their application; students who do not apply for aid upon admission are ineligible to receive institutional aid in subsequent years.
financial_aid.no_loans_note: Standard financial aid packages contain Stanford scholarships, federal/state grants, and work-study. No student loans are required.

under_100k.benefit: For families with typical assets and income below $100,000, Stanford expects no parent contribution toward educational costs. Students remain responsible for their own contribution from savings and employment.

under_150k.benefit: For families with typical assets and income below $150,000, Stanford states that the expected parent contribution is low enough for need-based aid and grants to cover tuition for students living on campus.

above_150k.benefit: Need-based scholarship aid scaled to family size, number of children in college, and demonstrated financial circumstances.

application_forms: FAFSA (US Citizens and Eligible Non-Citizens; School Code: 001305)
International Student Application for Financial Assistance (ISAFA) for eligible international students
financial_aid.income_thresholds_note: These income guidelines assume typical assets and US cost-of-living assumptions; Stanford says they may not apply to families living outside the United States.

phd_funding_guarantee.commitment: Stanford provides continuous 12-month funding to all enrolled PhD and DMA students in good academic standing for up to the first five years. The funding combination is tailored to the degree program.
components: Funding is provided through a combination of external fellowships, Stanford fellowships, research assistantships, and teaching assistantships; programs tailor the combination.
The commitment is funded at Stanford’s 20-hour-per-week Research Assistantship minimum; degree programs and faculty advisors arrange the support.
The university-wide policy does not prescribe one tuition unit load or a universal Cardinal Care subsidy; exact tuition and insurance treatment depends on the program and funding source.

scholarships_and_funding.name: Stanford Undergraduate Need-Based Financial Aid (International)
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: International applicants; citizenship and aid request are assessed under Stanford’s international policy
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: International applicants must request aid in the admission application. Stanford says aid request is a factor in the admission evaluation for international citizens; applicants admitted with aid requested are considered for full demonstrated need. Applicants who state they will not request aid and are admitted are generally ineligible to apply later during their four undergraduate years.

scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Institutional aid requires annual reapplication; check current-year rules.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: Limited institutional resources; aid request makes international admission more selective. Award rate not stated on the cited page.
scholarships_and_funding.deadline_timezone: US Pacific Time; exact hour not published
steps: Indicate on the Stanford first-year admission application that you are requesting financial aid; this request affects admission review for international citizens.

Separately submit the CSS Profile (school code 4704) and the International Student Supplement through Stanford Financial Aid document upload; Stanford identifies limited circumstances for the International Student Application for Financial Assistance as an alternative.
Submit any additional tax or supporting documents requested by the Financial Aid Office.
documents: Parent income and tax documentation if requested
Noncustodial Parent Waiver Request and supporting evidence only if applicable
scholarships_and_funding.application_process_note: International applicants must indicate on the admission application that they are requesting aid. Then submit the separate CSS Profile and International Student Supplement (or the approved alternative) and supporting financial documents; “separate” refers to these aid forms, not to the initial aid request.

scholarships_and_funding.name: Knight-Hennessy Scholars
scholarships_and_funding.program_scope: All full-time Stanford graduate degree programs, including the LLM, subject to current cohort eligibility and stated exceptions. KHS is a separate competitive award; it is not Stanford Law School funding.
scholarships_and_funding.applicant_scope: Applicants from all countries; first bachelor’s degree earned January 2020 or later (military service exception); must separately apply to and enroll in an eligible Stanford graduate degree
scholarships_and_funding.eligibility: For the 2027 cohort, applicants must apply to KHS and be admitted to and enroll in a full-time Stanford graduate degree starting in the same year, and meet the first-bachelor’s-date rule (January 2020 or later, with the military exception). KHS says there are no restrictions by field of study and lists eligible degrees including JD, MA, MBA, MD, MS, and PhD; its explicit exclusions do not include LLM. Selection is highly competitive and not guaranteed. For Stanford MBA applicants to the 2027 cohort, KHS eligibility requires submitting the MBA application by GSB Round 1 (2026-09-09); that date has passed as of 2026-09-24. Applicants who submitted by the deadline may continue their KHS application before the October 6 KHS deadline; this does not disqualify timely submitters.
scholarships_and_funding.coverage: Up to three years of tuition and associated fees, living and academic expenses, and annual travel stipend for selected KHS Scholars, subject to program eligibility and actual degree duration; not an automatic award or a net-price estimate.
scholarships_and_funding.renewal: Up to three years; not a general renewable award beyond the scholar’s eligible degree period.
scholarships_and_funding.competition: Highly selective; KHS publishes no formula or guaranteed qualifying score.
scholarships_and_funding.course_application_deadline: Stanford graduate program deadline; varies by program and may be earlier than 2026-12-01
steps: Submit the KHS application by October 6, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. Pacific Time.
Submit a separate Stanford graduate degree application by the earlier of the program deadline for KHS applicants or December 1, 2026.
For Stanford MBA applicants, submit the MBA application by GSB Round 1 (2026-09-09) to meet KHS eligibility; timely applicants may submit their KHS application by October 6, 2026.

fellowships_and_grants.award_coverage: 100% of demonstrated financial need with no required student loans. For families with typical assets, income below $100,000 means Stanford expects no parent contribution toward educational costs; students still have a student contribution. Income below $150,000 may qualify for need-based aid covering tuition for on-campus students. These thresholds may not apply to families living outside the United States.
fellowships_and_grants.eligibility_criteria: Admitted undergraduate students who apply for financial aid and demonstrate financial need.

record.description: Stanford University is a world-leading private research university located in California's Silicon Valley. Renowned for its entrepreneurial culture, academic excellence across undergraduate and graduate disciplines, groundbreaking research, and transformative financial aid, Stanford encompasses seven world-class schools: Humanities and Sciences, Engineering, Doerr School of Sustainability, Business (GSB), Law, Medicine, and Education.

factors_meta.method: Deterministic mapping from OpenAlex (research metrics), Open-Meteo geocoding/Wikidata (city population), official QS rank metadata where available, and tuition. Social/academic intensity is a UniSearch proxy signal, not an official university metric. Location axis is computed as city-life(0.0) <-> outside-major-city(1.0).

student_count.method: Direct student headcount published on Stanford Facts.

acceptance_rate_percent.method: Calculated from official CDS counts for Fall 2024 first-time first-year admission (2,067 admitted / 57,326 applicants).

tags.method: Derived from the official Stanford University overview of schools (Humanities and Sciences, Engineering, Medicine, Law, Education, Business) and private research university status.

admission_categories.label: Undergraduate First-Year Admission
admission_categories.description: One university-wide first-year application through the Common Application; applicants apply to Stanford, not to a selected major. SAT or ACT is required. Need-blind for US applicants; international applicants are need-aware if requesting aid.
extra_requirements: Common Application with Stanford Member Questions (3 short essays + 5 short answers)
$100 nonrefundable application fee or approved fee waiver
Official high school transcript covering grades 9-11 and mid-year senior grades
School Report and Counselor Recommendation letter
Two Teacher Evaluations strictly from core academic disciplines
SAT or ACT standardized test scores (official or self-reported for admission)

admission_categories.label: Stanford Law School JD Admission
admission_categories.description: Three-year Juris Doctor admission for Fall 2027 entry. Applicants submit through LSAC. The KHS-applicant completion cutoff is earlier than the regular JD deadline.
extra_requirements: Submit the JD application electronically through LSAC.
Pay the nonrefundable USD 85 Stanford Law application fee or request the Stanford Law fee waiver before submitting the application; allow 5–7 business days for a decision.
Submit a one-to-two-page resume and a personal statement of approximately two pages.
Complete Stanford Law’s required essay selection on the LSAC Letter of Recommendation form.
Submit valid LSAT or GRE General Test scores; LSAT applicants must also submit LSAT Argumentative Writing.
Arrange for required transcripts and recommendation letters through LSAC Credential Assembly Service.
admission_categories.deadline_status: Official current-cycle dates published by Stanford Law School.

requirement_profiles.label: JD applicant

requirement_profiles.requirements_note: Stanford requires a bachelor’s degree by enrollment and either LSAT or GRE. It publishes no minimum GPA or score guaranteeing admission.

admission_categories.label: Stanford School of Medicine MD Admission
admission_categories.description: MD admission uses the AMCAS primary application followed by an invitation-only Stanford Supplemental Application. The current official timeline lists recurring month-and-day dates but does not name an entry cycle; verify the dates against the intended AMCAS cycle.
admission_categories.application_fee_note: Stanford requires a nonrefundable supplemental application fee, but the current official page does not state its amount. The AAMC Fee Assistance Program waiver is available only to applicants approved before the primary application.
extra_requirements: Apply through the American Medical College Application Service (AMCAS).
Submit MCAT scores through the AMCAS process; check the current cycle page for the eligible test-date window.
Submit three to six letters of recommendation through AMCAS Letters Service.
After invitation, submit Stanford’s supplemental application, required essays, fee or applicable AAMC Fee Assistance Program waiver, and all required materials through the Stanford MD portal.
Do not send transcripts or letters directly to Stanford unless requested.

admission_categories.label: Stanford Undergraduate Transfer Admission
admission_categories.description: Transfer applicants apply through the Common Application to begin in the Fall quarter. Stanford’s official page lists recurring March 15 timing but does not name the entry cycle; confirm all dates and the application fee for the intended year.
admission_categories.application_fee_note: Stanford lists a USD 100 nonrefundable application fee and a fee-waiver request. The official page does not name an entry year for its recurring transfer dates.
extra_requirements: Submit the Common Application.
Submit ACT or SAT scores; Stanford reinstated the testing requirement beginning with the 2025–26 application cycle.
Submit the official high school transcript including graduation date and official transcripts from every college or university attended.
Submit the College Report completed by a school official at the current or most recent institution.
Submit letters of recommendation from two academic instructors.
Submit the USD 100 nonrefundable application fee or request a fee waiver.
